# Bar chart (`bar_chart`)

<!-- Generated by scripts/docs.js from schema.json. Edit the schema, then run `npm run docs`. -->

Compares values across categories, or across a short run of periods, with one or more series.

**Use when:** Comparing a measure across categories (revenue by rep, tickets by priority) or a short run of periods (revenue by quarter). Use horizontal bars for rankings and long names.

**Don't use when:** There is only one number (use kpi), the user needs exact values for many records (use table), or there are more than 30 categories (aggregate to top N first).

**Sizes:** M (default), L, full

## Fields

Fields from `id` to `note` are shared by every widget.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `"bar_chart"` | yes | Always "bar_chart". |
| `id` | string | yes | Unique id within the dashboard: lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens, e.g. "open-ar". |
| `title` | string | yes | What the widget shows, in sentence case with no trailing period, e.g. "Revenue by rep, Q3 2026". |
| `subtitle` | string |  | Optional one line of context under the title: scope, filter, or unit. |
| `size` | `"M"` \| `"L"` \| `"full"` |  | Width on the 12-column grid (S = 3, M = 6, L = 9, full = 12). Allowed: M, L, full. Default: `"M"`. |
| `note` | string |  | Optional footnote: caveats, definitions, or why data is missing. |
| `categories` | list of string | yes | Category labels in display order (top to bottom for horizontal bars). Sort rankings largest first; keep periods in time order. |
| `series` | list of object | yes | One entry per measure. Each series has exactly one value per category, in the same order as categories. |
| `series[].name` | string | yes | Series name shown in the legend and tooltip, e.g. "Revenue". |
| `series[].values` | list of number or null | yes | Raw numbers aligned with categories. Use null for a missing value, never 0. |
| `format` | `"number"` \| `"integer"` \| `"currency"` \| `"percent"` |  | How values are displayed on the axis and tooltip. percent expects fractions: 0.45 shows as 45%. Default: `"number"`. |
| `orientation` | `"vertical"` \| `"horizontal"` |  | vertical for periods and a few short categories; horizontal for rankings, many categories, or long names. Default: `"vertical"`. |
| `stacked` | boolean |  | Stack series into one bar per category. Only when the series add up to a meaningful total (new + renewal revenue). Default: `false`. |

## Example

```json
{
  "type": "bar_chart",
  "id": "revenue-by-quarter",
  "title": "Revenue by quarter",
  "subtitle": "Hardware and services, last 6 quarters",
  "size": "M",
  "format": "currency",
  "categories": ["Q2 2025", "Q3 2025", "Q4 2025", "Q1 2026", "Q2 2026", "Q3 2026"],
  "series": [
    { "name": "Hardware", "values": [182000, 240500, 198300, 156900, 214700, 263100] },
    { "name": "Services", "values": [64200, 71800, 69500, 73100, 80400, 88900] }
  ],
  "stacked": true
}
```

## Checks beyond the schema

- Error when a series has a different number of values than there are categories.
- Error when two series share a name.
- Warns when percent values look like whole numbers (45 instead of 0.45).
- Warns when vertical bars have more than 8 categories or labels longer than 14 characters (use horizontal).
- Warns when stacked is true with only one series.
